newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - July 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - July 2.

text.p: THE DOMINION

Code aimed at all parents -- Sowry: The government did not intend using benefit cuts or reductions as a persuasion within the new code of social responsibility it was developing, Social Welfare Minister Roger Sowry said on Tuesday. Page 1.

English casts doubt on benefits of free GP visits: Health Minister Bill English appears to be at odds with NZ First over the benefits of a free medical care scheme introduced on Tuesday for children under six. Page 2.

Shirley gives details on welfare allegation: Information about allegations that Auckland child welfare staff falsified documents has been provided to the retired judge looking into whether there is enough substance to the claims to force an inquiry. Page 2.

Manufacturers of automotive parts being 'ignored': The government was ignoring the impact the loss of the assembly industry would have on about 5000 people inolved in manufacturing components, Automotive Component Manufacturers Association president David Tibby said on Tuesday. Page 12.

Textile tariff cuts draw industry's fire: The government was, in effect, sacking 10,000 apparel and textile workers by pushing through tariff reductions while not cutting compliance costs for business, Apparel and Textile Federation chief executive Marcia Dunnett said on Tuesday. Page 12.
THE PRESS

Winebox fraud claims not proved: New Zealand First leader Winston Peters's lawyer conceded on Tuesday that the Winebox documents contained no evidence of corruption, fraud, or conspiracy in the Serious Fraud Office or in the Inland Revenue Department. Page 1.
Damage accident, MP says: Taxpayers may be asked to foot a bill of more than $257 for damage in a Melbourne hotel room occupied by New Zealand First MP Rana Waitai last month. Page 1.

Aotearoa TV loses struggle for survival: The plug was pulled on Aotearoa Television Network on Tuesday after the troubled channel lost its frequency and ran out of funds to pay for transmission services. Page 6.
Govt to be sued on hepatitis: More than 100 people infected with hepatitis C through contaminated blood and blood products are going to sue the government. Page 6.
Community Trust boosts earnings: Trust Bank Canterbury Community Trust lifted pre-tax earnings about 150 percent in its first year after selling its Trust Bank New Zealand shareholding. Page 30.

Court bid to lift payout to Equiticorp: Equiticorp statutory managers have lodged documents in the Court of Appeal in Wellington seeking to incrase the amount to be paid to Equiticorp by the Crown in the New Zealand Steel case. Page 28.
THE NEW ZEALAND HERALD
Hong Kong 'sulking' provokes Peters rebuke: The Deputy Prime Minister Winston Peters has condemned the "sulky" British stance at the Hong Kong handover, branding it as "ungenerous" and pre-planned.

Liquidators chasing Best Buy man: Computer retailer Best Buy, which shut its doors last Thursday leaving scores of customers owed thousands of dollars, is also embroiled in litigation relating to its past involvement in PC retailer Cost Club.

Fernz waits on French approvals: Fernz Corporation expects to know early next week if French stock exchange officials have approved its bid for Paris-based chemicals company Compagnie Francaise des Products Industriels.

Cellphone data use set to rise: Data transmission on New Zealand's cellphone networks is set for meteoric growth, potentially accounting for more than half the cellular traffic by the end of the century.
Weyerhaeuser plans plant: Weyerhaeuser of the United States plans to build a timber manufacturing plant near the Nelson forests it bought a share of in April.
--Wellington Newsroom (64 4) 4734746
